Just use an svg with sane with and height values. There is no gain in using raster graphics of enourmous size if it's a rendered vector. It's actually of worse quality at a much bigger size.

It's actually of worse quality at a much bigger size.

Really? It looks the same for me.

That's the difference between raster images (jpg, gif, png, bmp,...) and vector images (svg, ai,...). Raster images only look good until some resolution, vector images you can zoom in to infinity without a quality loss.

But vector images only work on images defined points and curves, and don't work well for photos or other images which aren't easily broken down in simple geometric forms.
